ranked_open_corpus_matches.source: Qubbet el-Hawa 26 (Sabni), tomb façade inscription A
ranked_open_corpus_matches.attested_sequence_summary: A message reports the sole companion and lector-priest Mekhu dead; Sabni describes a troop of his funerary estate and 100 donkeys carrying oil, honey, clothing, faience and another oil/product toward foreign lands; he writes that he set forth to bring back his father who had travelled to Wawat, and later states that he had him transported with the aid of his troops.
ranked_open_corpus_matches.friend_caveat: smr-wꜥ.tj is an Egyptian title 'sole companion', not proof of modern personal friendship.

ranked_open_corpus_matches.source: Papyrus Chester Beatty III Dream Book, BM EA 10683
ranked_open_corpus_matches.attested_sequence_summary: The manuscript is an Egyptian dream manual organized by the repeated frame 'If a man sees himself in a dream ...'. Open-access museum records confirm the dream-book context; known entries contain domestic, travel, fire and other motifs, but no single open-access entry located in this pass reproduces the full friend + home token + loading + winged vehicle + foreign land + return chain.

janus_bidirectional_audit.promotion_rule: Do not promote to SINGLE_ANCIENT_PROCESS_MATCH unless one ancient local text/procedure independently closes DREAM/ORIGIN + LOAD/CARGO + COMPANION/HELP + FOREIGN-LAND TRANSFER + RETURN/PRESERVED-HOME edges without importing steps from unrelated sources.

most_interesting_result.summary: The strongest newly found independent parallel is Sabni: companion-title + textiles/oils/goods carried toward foreign lands + journey to bring back a father + transport. The strongest reverse mirror is Punt: foreign land -> load ships -> return home in peace. Sinuhe independently supplies the HOME -> FOREIGN LAND -> HOME_PRIME semantic loop. Together they map much of the modern dream decomposition, but they remain three different ancient sources and therefore cannot be fused into one ancient version of the dream.

supported: Independent open-access Egyptian records contain strong partial structural parallels to several nodes of the decomposed dream.
Sabni contains an unusually dense cluster of companion-title, carried goods including cloth and oils, foreign lands, father-recovery journey and transport.
The Punt scenes explicitly place loading ships and returning home from a foreign land in sequence.
Sinuhe strongly parallels the semantic home-exile-return loop.
not_supported: The friend's dream is an ancient Egyptian text or prophecy.
The ancient texts describe an aircraft or motorhome.
The separate Sabni, Punt, Sinuhe and Dream Book records may be merged into one historical procedure.
Lexical or structural similarity demonstrates transmission, prediction or supernatural causation.
